description: The toolchain that turns code into running software: Git from first commit to rebase, pull-request workflows, continuous integration, containers, automated testing and deployment, and the monitoring that tells you when to roll back. Taught to the depth of industry DevOps practice.
modelledOn: Kim, Humble, Debois and Willis, The DevOps Handbook
Beyer, Jones, Petoff and Murphy, Site Reliability Engineering
outcomes: Use Git fluently: commits, branches, merges, rebases, tags, stashes and history rewriting, and explain the object model behind them.
Collaborate through remote repositories with pull requests, code review and a branching strategy.
Resolve merge conflicts and recover from mistakes with reflog, revert and reset.
Build a continuous integration pipeline that lints, tests and packages a project on every push.
Containerise an application with Docker and compose multi-service environments.
Deploy automatically to a host, monitor it with logs and metrics, and roll back safely.

units.title: Why version control and the Git model
topics: The problem: copies of copies, lost work, who changed what; centralised versus distributed VCS
Git's object model: blobs, trees, commits, refs; the working tree, index and repository
Installing Git, configuring identity, the command line and a GUI client
Shell basics needed for the course: paths, pipes, environment variables

units.title: Git basics: commit, branch, merge
topics: init, status, add, commit; good commit messages; .gitignore
log, diff, show; inspecting history; blame
Branches as pointers; checkout and switch; fast-forward and three-way merges
Tags, stash, amend; undoing with restore, revert and reset (soft, mixed, hard)
Rebase versus merge; interactive rebase to clean history; reflog as the safety net

units.title: Remote repositories and pull requests
topics: clone, fetch, pull, push; remotes and tracking branches; SSH keys and tokens
GitHub and GitLab: issues, pull or merge requests, reviews, protected branches
Forking workflow for open source; feature-branch and trunk-based development; GitFlow compared
Code review practice: small changes, checklists, constructive comments
Semantic versioning and releases

units.title: Resolving conflicts and collaboration failures
topics: How conflicts arise; reading conflict markers; resolving in the editor and with a merge tool
Conflicts during rebase and cherry-pick; rerere
Recovering lost commits, fixing a bad merge, splitting and squashing commits
Team exercise: four people, one repository, deliberate conflicts

units.title: Automated testing
topics: Unit, integration and end-to-end tests; the testing pyramid; test runners for Python, JavaScript and Java
Linting and formatting as automated checks; pre-commit hooks
Code coverage and its limits; flaky tests
Test-driven development in a small kata

units.title: Continuous integration pipelines
topics: CI principles: every push builds and tests; fast feedback; the build must stay green
GitHub Actions: workflows, jobs, steps, matrices, caching, secrets; GitLab CI compared
Pipeline stages: lint, test, build, package, publish artefacts
Status checks on pull requests; badges; notifications
Reproducible builds and dependency pinning; software supply-chain basics

units.title: Containers
topics: Why containers: environment drift; images versus containers; namespaces and cgroups in brief
Docker: Dockerfile, layers, build, run, volumes, networks, environment variables
Multi-stage builds and small images; registries and tagging
Docker Compose for an app with a database and a cache
Introduction to Kubernetes: pods, deployments, services; when it is overkill

units.title: Automated deployment
topics: Environments: development, staging, production; configuration and secrets management
Deploying a web app to a VPS, a PaaS and a static host from CI; infrastructure as code with Terraform or Ansible in brief
Deployment strategies: rolling, blue-green, canary; database migrations
Continuous delivery versus continuous deployment; release gates and approvals

units.title: Monitoring and rollback
topics: Logs, metrics and traces; structured logging; Prometheus and Grafana or a hosted equivalent
Health checks, uptime monitoring, alerting and on-call basics
Service level indicators and objectives; error budgets
Rolling back a bad release: image tags, reverting commits, feature flags; blameless post-mortems

units.title: DevOps culture and capstone
topics: The DORA metrics: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore
DevSecOps: dependency scanning, secret scanning, container scanning in the pipeline
Capstone: take a small application from repository to monitored deployment with a full pipeline
Working with low bandwidth: shallow clones, partial clones, caching, offline-first workflows

schedule.title: Why version control and Git internals
schedule.exercise: Explain, with a diagram, how Git stores a commit as blobs, trees and a commit object and what the index is for.

tasks.title: Make a commit, then use cat-file to inspect its commit, tree and blob objects and show how their hashes link
Configure Git identity, create a repository and make three commits, then verify author details with git log
Use pipes, environment variables and paths to count the commits per author in a log and save the result to a file

schedule.title: Everyday Git and branching
schedule.exercise: Write a short guide on good commit messages with three before and after examples.

tasks.title: Initialise a repository, add a .gitignore, stage and commit three files with clear messages, and check status after each step
Use log, diff, show and blame to find which commit introduced a given line and who wrote it
Create two branches, make a fast-forward merge and a three-way merge, and draw the resulting commit graph from log output

schedule.title: Undoing and rewriting history
schedule.exercise: Explain which command you would use to undo a pushed commit versus a local commit, and why.

tasks.title: Stash work in progress, switch branches, restore it, tag a release and amend the last commit message
Undo changes with restore, revert and reset in soft, mixed and hard modes, and record what each does to the working tree and index
Clean five messy commits with an interactive rebase, then recover a commit dropped by mistake using reflog

schedule.title: Remotes, collaboration and review
schedule.exercise: Describe the branching workflow you would give a team of five on a school project, and why.

tasks.title: Clone a repository, make a branch, push it to a remote and set the tracking branch, then pull a colleague's change
Run the forking workflow: fork, branch, commit, push and prepare a pull request with a clear description
Tag releases with semantic versioning across three changes (patch, minor, major) and write release notes from the commit log

schedule.title: Merge conflicts
schedule.exercise: Write a conflict-resolution checklist and use it on the conflict from the team exercise.

tasks.title: Create and resolve a merge conflict in one file by reading the markers, and check the final content by running the tests
Resolve conflicts during a rebase and a cherry-pick of three commits, and enable rerere to reuse a resolution
Recover from a bad merge and a lost branch with reflog, then split one large commit into two clean commits

schedule.title: Automated testing
schedule.exercise: Design a test plan for a small grading function, labelling which tests are unit, integration and end-to-end.

tasks.title: Write five unit tests for a grading function including boundary values and run them with a test runner
Add a linter and formatter with a pre-commit hook that blocks a commit with a style error, and show it blocking one
Build a function from scratch using test-driven development over six red-green-refactor cycles, and report coverage and one flaky test fix

schedule.title: Continuous integration
schedule.exercise: Draw the stages of a CI pipeline for a web app and mark where a failure should stop the run.

tasks.title: Run the tests, a linter and a build in sequence from a script, stopping at the first failure and reporting the failing stage
Write a workflow with a test matrix on two language versions, dependency caching and a secret, and read its job log
Create a pipeline with lint, test, build, package and publish stages and diagnose a red stage from seeded errors

schedule.title: Pull request checks and supply chain
schedule.exercise: Write the branch protection rules and status checks you would require for the main branch.

tasks.title: Configure required status checks so a pull request with failing tests cannot merge, and show the block
Pin dependencies with a lock file, rebuild twice and compare results to show the build is reproducible
Audit a project's dependencies for a vulnerable and an abandoned package, replace one, and confirm the tests still pass

schedule.title: Containers and Docker
schedule.exercise: Explain environment drift with an example from your own project and how a container removes it.

tasks.title: Show that two containers share the host kernel but see separate process lists, and compare with a virtual machine
Write a Dockerfile for a small app, build it, run it with a volume, an environment variable and a published port, and test it with curl
Convert a 1 GB image to a multi-stage build under 100 MB, tag it with a version and push it to a registry

schedule.title: Compose and Kubernetes basics
schedule.exercise: Argue whether a three-person start-up needs Kubernetes, listing what Compose cannot do for them.

tasks.title: Run an app, a database and a cache with Compose, and show data survives a restart of the app container
Fix a Compose file with wrong network names and a missing volume that stops the app reaching the database
Deploy a pod, scale a deployment to three replicas, expose it with a service, and kill a pod to watch it return

schedule.title: Deployment and delivery strategies
schedule.exercise: Choose a deployment strategy for a database change on a busy payments app, and write the rollback plan.

tasks.title: Set different configuration and secrets for development and production using environment files, without committing a secret
Deploy a web app to a VPS from CI over SSH and verify the new version responds
Compare rolling, blue-green and canary releases of a service, measure errors seen by users during each, and choose one with a migration step

schedule.title: Monitoring, incidents and rollback
schedule.exercise: Write a blameless post-mortem for a failed release using the timeline of an incident.

tasks.title: Add structured logs and a health endpoint to a service, then find a failing request by searching the logs
Compute an availability SLI and error budget from 30 days of request logs and decide whether to freeze releases
Roll back a bad release by reverting a commit and redeploying a previous image tag, and record time to restore

schedule.title: DORA metrics, DevSecOps and capstone
schedule.exercise: Prepare a short review of your capstone pipeline using the four DORA metrics and a list of improvements.

tasks.title: Compute deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore from a log of 40 deployments
Add secret scanning, dependency scanning and container scanning to a pipeline, and fix the findings in a seeded repository
Take a small app from repository to monitored deployment with a CI pipeline, container build, staged release, health checks and a rollback test
